components: Registry-free CLI and private internal package
Release build, checksum, SBOM, provenance, signature, and independent-review gates
GitHub Actions validation and CodeQL workflows
Transactional project creation, adoption, rollback, and recovery
Schema-governed reports, skill catalog, and shipped templates
environments: GitHub-hosted Windows, Linux, and macOS runners
excluded: Live Azure resources and deployed workload posture
Remote mutation, release publication, and package promotion

evidence: Transactional adoption journals, locks, rollback, and recovery are documented in docs/THREAT-MODEL.md and exercised by npm run check.
The current unsigned candidate verifies 150 checksum-covered files.
Local security and Gitleaks scans pass with pinned tools and immutable workflow actions.
Production verification requires trusted RSA signatures and independently signed review evidence.
Read-only GitHub inspection found no main-branch protection or rulesets and disabled hosted secret/dependency protections.
The package has zero runtime dependencies and no always-on service cost.
Hosted validation uses bounded jobs and retention windows; no deployment resources are part of this package release.
JSON schemas, immutable execution snapshots, release checks, and 43 skill contracts provide deterministic operations evidence.
Remote HEAD has a successful nine-run OS/Node matrix, but current uncommitted candidate changes have not run remotely.
Repository scans and project discovery are bounded; the complete local gate passes within its configured CI timeout.
No application runtime or deployed service performance is in scope.

findings.title: Hosted source changes do not require an independent human review
findings.impact: Automated Security Validation and CodeQL checks are enforced, but the sole write-capable maintainer can still merge a change without a second person reviewing it. This leaves human design and intent defects outside automated coverage.
findings.recommendation: Add a distinct qualified collaborator or team, then require at least one approving review for main and assign CODEOWNERS for workflows, release scripts, security policy, and audit contracts.
tradeOffs: A second trusted maintainer adds coordination and merge latency.
Enabling a required review before adding that identity would lock out the sole maintainer.
The separately signed release-review gate remains mandatory even after source review is enforced.
evidence: Main protection now requires strict Aggregate cross-platform evidence and JavaScript security analysis checks with admin enforcement, linear history, conversation resolution, and no force pushes or deletions.
Secret scanning, push protection, Dependabot security updates, vulnerability alerts, automated fixes, and private vulnerability reporting are enabled.
Actions are restricted to GitHub-owned actions and CodeQL reports zero open alerts after reviewed dispositions.
The repository has one write-capable collaborator, so required_pull_request_reviews remains unset; SECURITY.md requires independent review before production release.

limitations: This is a design-time review; no Azure environment or package deployment was accessed.
Non-provider secret patterns and validity checks remain unavailable or disabled after best-effort enablement.
No second qualified reviewer identity or trusted release-signing identity is currently provisioned.
